decision.summary: A confirmed temporary offset exists in E/U around 430–440: E spikes positive, U dips negative, both partially recover by 440. The N rise starting at ~420 persists through 465 with no return observed in allowed context, so its status remains uncertain as a temporary offset. No other temporary intervals are supported by axis-consistent onset/return evidence within [385,500].

intervals.observation: E-component shows a positive transient spike peaking near index 432–434, with U-component showing a concurrent negative dip (minimum near 434–436); both return toward pre-event levels by ~440. N-component continues monotonic rise throughout and does not participate in the transient offset.

N-component exhibits sustained monotonic rise from ~420 onward; no opposing return observed within allowed context (up to 500), and interior is smooth without reversal. Thus, no temporary offset interval can be confirmed for N.
